title: AtlasOps service-health dashboard
context: Build the first AtlasOps service-health workflow and prove it handles real network, cache, and provider behavior without leaking credentials, hiding freshness, or confusing the user.

stories.title: Implement the server-side provider adapter
stories.outcome: Provider behavior is isolated behind a validated internal contract.
stories.context: The browser must not receive provider credentials or provider-specific response complexity.
acceptanceCriteria: Server adapter constructs requests and handles timeout and non-success status
Runtime validation rejects malformed provider data
Provider response is mapped to the milestone 5 normalized type
Unit tests use synthetic fixtures and make no paid network calls
stories.dataContract: Use the approved normalized contract from SWAI-304.

expectations.security: Credential is server-only and redacted from errors.
expectations.privacy: Return only fields required by the UI.
expectations.accessibility: Adapter errors map to actionable UI categories.
expectations.analytics: Track duration/status category without payload content.

definitionOfDone: Fixture tests cover success, empty, malformed, 401, 429, timeout, outage

stories.title: Build the primary dashboard workflow
stories.outcome: The user can make the decision identified in milestone 5 using current, understandable data.
stories.context: Implement the approved flow with URL/shareable state where appropriate and without speculative secondary features.
acceptanceCriteria: Initial, loading, result, empty, stale, partial, and error states are intentionally designed
Filters or pagination remain keyboard accessible and preserve understandable URL state
Data freshness and source are visible
Mobile and desktop layouts preserve the primary decision
designRefs: Your approved user flow and wireframe

expectations.security: No direct browser call requiring secret.
expectations.privacy: Do not persist query data beyond the declared need.
expectations.accessibility: Status announcements, labels, focus, non-color meaning.
expectations.analytics: Track workflow completion and error category only.

stories.title: Prevent failed responses from becoming cached data
stories.outcome: A provider failure cannot appear as a valid stale success.
stories.context: QA observed that a failed response is normalized to an empty array and cached, hiding the outage until cache expiry.
acceptanceCriteria: Provider failure remains distinguishable from a valid empty result
Only accepted successful data is cached
A regression test fails before and passes after the fix
stories.dataContract: Result type distinguishes success, empty success, and failure.

expectations.analytics: Outage is an operational error, not empty-result product telemetry.

definitionOfDone: Regression test and production-like verification pass
stories.seededBug: Catch every adapter error and return an empty array, then cache that value. Replace this with a typed failure path.

stories.title: Deploy and document provider operations
stories.outcome: The dashboard can be operated within provider limits and switched off safely.
stories.context: Document local/preview/production configuration, rate-limit behavior, cost monitoring, cache rules, provider status response, and rollback.
acceptanceCriteria: Production deployment is verified with synthetic use
Runbook states credential ownership, limits, cost alert, cache/freshness, outage behavior, and disable/rollback steps
README links the ADR and documents known limitations
